what_the_gate_9_harness_actually_is.transport: Playwright/Chromium against https://homesignal.net; every DB read is an HTTP request to PostgREST made by the page's own supabase-js anon client
what_the_gate_9_harness_actually_is.evidence: the file imports { chromium } from 'playwright' and nothing else network-facing; repo-wide grep for a pg client (require('pg') | from 'pg' | new Client() ) returns 0 files; the repo ships no package.json, so there is no postgres dependency to configure
what_the_gate_9_harness_actually_is.consequence: there is no harness-owned Postgres connection on which application_name can be set. PostgREST names its own pooled backends.

permission_probe_run_as_anon.why_anon: anon is the only role the harness ever authenticates as

exact_permission_missing.grant: membership in the built-in role pg_read_all_stats (or superuser) for the role the harness runs as
exact_permission_missing.without_it: pg_stat_activity.query is returned as the literal '<insufficient privilege>' and state / wait_event / query_start / xact_start are NULL for every session but the caller's own

why_task_2_cannot_run: TASK 2a requires capturing query, state, wait_event, xact_start, query_start, pid, application_name. Five of those seven are invisible to the harness role for every other session.

TASK 2e's BLOCKED-ON-ENVIRONMENT rule requires matching other sessions' query text against 'app_projects_for_zip' OR 'app_zip_projects_markers'. That column reads '<insufficient privilege>' for all 47 other sessions, so the rule is not evaluable by the harness.

TASK 1's application_name tagging has no connection to apply to, and the two ways to create one are both unauthorized here: granting pg_read_all_stats to the public anon role would let any anon caller read every session's SQL, and giving the harness its own Postgres connection requires a database credential that does not exist as a CI secret today.
